# Sell all 200.00 USD the book holds after a 100.00 USD invoice was overpaid
# with 200.00 USD: 100 against the invoice's own basis, 100 against the credit
# the overpayment left. Both were carried at 1.40, so the cost released is
# 140.00 + 140.00 = 280.00 CAD, and the 290.00 CAD the sale fetched leaves
# $residual$ booking a 10.00 CAD gain.
#
# Nothing here is special to an overpayment: a basis is a basis, and a sale
# names the ones it measures against. The point of the fixture is that the
# second 100.00 USD can be sold at all — before the credit opened a basis, the
# book held 200.00 USD and would only let 100.00 of it go.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-03-01 * "Sell 200 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD -100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.40"
		value: "-140.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{basis_a}"
	Assets:Bank:USD -100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.40"
		value: "-140.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{basis_b}"
	Assets:Bank 290.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "290.00"
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
